title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Joint Retainers - Confidentiality Conflict
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is acting for two partners (Client A and Client B) under a joint retainer in a breach of contract claim. Client A calls the paralegal privately and admits they secretly siphoned funds from the partnership, instructing the paralegal not to tell Client B. What is the paralegal's **first action**?
options: Disclose the information to Client B immediately, as there is no confidentiality between joint clients.
Advise Client A that information cannot be kept secret from Client B in a joint retainer, and if Client A refuses to allow disclosure, the paralegal must withdraw from representing both.
Keep the secret and withdraw only from representing Client B.
Report Client A to the police for theft and withdraw from the file entirely.
questions.explain: Under Rule 3.04, when acting for joint clients, no information received from one client can be treated as confidential from the other. If one client requires information to be withheld from the other, a conflict arises. The first step is to advise the client of this rule. If they still refuse disclosure, the paralegal must withdraw from representing both clients.
